rules.title: Prohibition on Providing Algorithmic Devices to Landlords
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for any person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord.
rules.exemptions: An algorithmic device does not include software or a product used to publish reports regarding rental rates or occupancy levels from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old or from information available to the general public, that does not recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for future leases or renewals. [§ 98.1102(a)]; An algorithmic device does not include software or a product used by a person to establish rental rates or income limits in accordance with local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines. [§ 98.1102(b)]
rules.quoted_span:
(a) It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an
algorithmic device to a landlord.

rules.title: Prohibition on Landlord Use of Algorithmic Devices
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property. Each month a violation continues and each residential rental property for which an algorithmic device is used constitutes a separate and distinct violation.
rules.exemptions: An algorithmic device does not include software or a product used to publish reports regarding rental rates or occupancy levels from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old or from information available to the general public, that does not recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for future leases or renewals. [§ 98.1102(a)]; An algorithmic device does not include software or a product used by a person to establish rental rates or income limits in accordance with local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines. [§ 98.1102(b)]
rules.quoted_span:
(b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
For each month a violation of section 98.1103(b) exists or continues, and
for each residential rental property a landlord uses an algorithmic device,
it shall constitute a separate and distinct violation.

rules.title: Tenant Remedies and Civil Penalties for Algorithmic Rent-Setting
rules.requirement: A tenant may bring a civil action against a landlord for injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation of Division 11. A prevailing tenant is entitled to recover costs and reasonable attorney's fees, and lease provisions limiting a tenant's attorney fee recovery are unenforceable.
rules.interaction: The remedies under section 98.1104 are cumulative and are in addition to any other remedies in Division 11 or at law, statute, or ordinance.
rules.quoted_span:
( a ) A tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to
$1,000 per violation of this Division, in a civil action against a landlord.
In an action brought under this Division, a prevailing tenant shall recover
costs and reasonable attorney’s fees. A prevailing tenant includes a tenant
granted an order for injunctive relief. A lease provision that limits a tenant
from recovering attorney’s fees shall not be enforceable against a tenant’s
claim for attorney’s fees that arise under this Division.

scope_mappings.statement: An algorithmic device does not include software or a product used by a person to establish rental rates or income limits in accordance with local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines.
scope_mappings.scope_words:
Algorithmic device does not include either of
the following:
scope_mappings.condition_evidence:
Algorithmic device does not include either of
the following:
(a) A software or product used by a person to publish reports regarding rental
rates or occupancy levels from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor
data that is more than 90 days old, or from information available to the
general public, and does not recommend rental rates or occupancy levels
for future residential rental property leases or renewals.
(b) A software or product used by a person to establish rental rates or income
limits in accordance with local, state, or federal affordable housing
program guidelines.
scope_mappings.target_anchor: ( a ) A tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or
scope_mappings.target_quote:
( a ) A tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to
$1,000 per violation of this Division, in a civil action against a landlord.
In an action brought under this Division, a prevailing tenant shall recover
costs and reasonable attorney’s fees. A prevailing tenant includes a tenant
granted an order for injunctive relief. A lease provision that limits a tenant
from recovering attorney’s fees shall not be enforceable against a tenant’s
claim for attorney’s fees that arise under this Division.

decision.reason: Section 98.1104(a) establishes civil remedies, damages, penalties, and fee recovery rather than defining or restricting the use of algorithmic devices.
